node.statement: Let B be that convex coordinate box and let z,z' in B. Since the domain and codomain split as icalH direct-sum calH and alpha+beta is the canonical identification with calX, identify the identity derivative with (alpha,beta) maps to alpha+beta. Along gamma(t)=z'+t(z-z'), the Banach-space fundamental theorem of calculus gives p_V(z)-p_V(z')-(z-z')=integral_0^1 (Dp_V(gamma(t))-I)(z-z') dt, hence its norm is at most theta||z-z'||. Therefore (1-theta)||z-z'||<=||p_V(z)-p_V(z')||<=(1+theta)||z-z'||, proving injectivity and bi-Lipschitz control. At each z, Dp_V(z)=I+E_z with ||E_z||<=theta<1, so the norm-convergent Neumann series sum_{n>=0}(-E_z)^n is its inverse and has norm at most (1-theta)^{-1}. The finite-dimensional C^1 inverse function theorem makes p_V a local C^1 diffeomorphism. Injectivity makes the local inverses agree on overlaps; since a local diffeomorphism is open, these glue to a C^1 inverse on p_V(B), so p_V:B to p_V(B) is a C^1 diffeomorphism.
